120ms per symbol + 40ms gap, about 5-6 symbols/s; a space is 240ms of silence.
Waiting for DTMF signal — point another device\'s speaker at this mic
Decoded characters appear line by line here after listening starts
A symbol is confirmed after 3 frames (~120ms); silence over 160ms inserts a space, 600ms starts a new line. Only sound actually heard by this mic can be demodulated.
Column freqs 1209 / 1336 / 1477 / 1633 Hz, row freqs 697 / 770 / 852 / 941 Hz. Each symbol is a dual tone: one row + one column.
TX supports 0-9, A-D, *, # and space; lowercase is uppercased automatically; other letters and punctuation are skipped.
Phone speaker to mic: fairly stable within 1-3 m in quiet rooms; farther or noisy rooms drop symbols.
About 5 symbols/s (120ms symbol + 40ms gap); long messages take patience.
Sound is not encrypted: any device that can hear it can decode it — never use for secrets or sensitive data.
Recognition depends on mic and speaker hardware; the level bar maps relative dBFS and is not calibrated.
